subject: Currents AI: Implementation & Cost-Performance Calibration

Subject: Re: Currents AI pilot — next steps on tuning and SLA

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. Diego and I walked out of it excited, but before we lock in the pilot we need a concrete plan for how Redwood will help us meet our cost and latency targets during the onboarding window. Two things we care about up front:

- Keep 95th percentile generation latency < 450ms for our 1–2k rpm baseline.
- Keep per-1k-request cost below $4 during the pilot.

Can you send a short implementation checklist that covers batching, caching, quantization guidance, and routing policy options? We have a rough sample of our request mix (attached) and procurement will need a scope doc + initial SLA draft to move forward.

Attaching: pilot_scope.xlsx (high-level ask), currents-traffic-sample.json

— Sam

Subject: Re: Currents AI pilot — next steps on tuning and SLA

Hi Sam —

Appreciate the clarity. I've looped in Monica (CS engineer) and Priyom (solutions) — they'll own the technical runbook and routing plan respectively. Below is a concise onboarding checklist we can expand into the pilot scope doc and the SLA draft (attached).

Quick intake (items we need from Currents):
- Confirmation of steady-state RPM and peak burst (we saw sample but want daily windows).
- 95/99 latency SLOs by route (chat vs batch embeddings).
- Example prompts & max token lengths.
- Any data retention/KMS constraints that affect caching.

Initial tuning plan (high level):
1) Batching: start with adaptive batching target sizes: chat=8–12, embeddings=16–32 depending on token distribution; we will instrument P95/P99 in the first 48h and adjust.
2) KV/prefix caching: enable prefix cache for repeated system prompts and large context segments (recommended TTL=3h during pilot unless you require shorter retention).
3) Quantization profile: begin with q4f16 for base generation; if hallucination risk is high for any route we’ll try q8_0 for that model variant. Monica will provide a quick A/B checklist to validate quality regressions.
4) Routing policy: primary route to optimized medium-cost variant, fallback to high-accuracy variant on quality alerts, and fallback to regional replica if capacity triggers. Priyom will propose a canary rollout policy for gradual cutover.

Deliverables before pilot start (we’ll compile these into one package):
- Pilot scope + SLA draft (attached).
- Implementation runbook with rollbacks, metrics to track, and alert thresholds.
- Test harness for your team (traffic-replay + synthetic spike tests).

Next steps: can we do a 30-min technical sync on Mon 14 Sep at 11:00am PT? If that works, Monica and Priyom will bring an initial config and we’ll put the SLA into DocuSign-ready state.

Attachments: SLA-draft.pdf, pilot_scope.xlsx

Best,
Avery Johnson

Subject: Re: Currents AI pilot — next steps on tuning and SLA

Hi Sam —

Posting the technical checklist here so the sync has a concrete starting point. I'll lead the 14th sync and bring baseline configs we can deploy in a sandbox.

Technical checklist (sandbox -> pilot):
- Ingest & validate traffic sample (I used currents-traffic-sample.json). Key metrics: avg tokens/request, token length distribution, percent of same-prefix requests.
- Baseline profile: run model at q4f16, batch sizes=8 chat / 16 embeddings, KV cache enabled with TTL=3h, warmup=50 requests per worker. Measure P95 and cost per 1k.
- Quality validation: create 100 prompt test set from your sample. Run generation at q4f16 vs q8_0 and flag delta in BLEU/ROUGE/specific hallucination checks; if delta>threshold we keep q8_0 for that route.
- Batching instrumentation: enable per-route batching histograms and token-level cost reporting. We recommend starting with max-batch-delay=10ms and increase only if latency SLO met comfortably.
- Routing & fallback rules (initial):
  - Route A (default): optimized CPU/GPU mix variant (lower cost)
  - Route B (quality): high-accuracy variant (higher cost) triggered by quality regression or manual override
  - Emergency fallback: regional replica (same model) if primary capacity falls below 30%
- Canary plan: 10% traffic -> 30% -> 100% over 48–72h with rollback thresholds at P95>550ms or cost/1k>1.5x target during canary.

Operational notes:
- If your prompts include long user histories, recommend enabling per-request KV caching for recent user tokens (we'll provide a small snippet to update client-side headers).
- Quantization tradeoffs: q4f16 generally gives best cost/latency balance; use q8_0 only for routes requiring strict output fidelity after A/B validation.

I'll attach the short A/B checklist and a minimal test harness script in the shared Drive during the sync.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Currents AI pilot — next steps on tuning and SLA

Adding routing and rollout specifics we should commit to for the pilot. I built these as actionable knobs so procurement can see concrete rollback/limits in the SLA.

Routing knobs to include in implementation runbook:
- Traffic weight ceilings per route (start default route <= 80% during canary).
- Cost-governor: auto-shift to cheaper model variant when 5-min rolling cost/1k exceeds threshold; lock out auto-shift for routes flagged as "quality-sensitive".
- Latency-aware routing: measure P95 per 1m window; if P95 rises >100ms vs baseline for 3 consecutive windows, shift 20% traffic to regional replica.
- Autoscale buffer policy: maintain 25% spare capacity to absorb bursts for the pilot; documented SLA exception for first 72h as we calibrate.

I also attached a sample HST (HubSpot) deal link and a short snippet for the routes we want to expose in your dashboard (so your SREs can see when shifts happen).

— Priyom
Priyom Das
